summary: The note surveys school safety and anti-bullying initiatives launched in schools across Canada, Japan, Ireland, Brazil, the UK and the USA between September 2023 and February 2024. Approaches range from awareness programs and biometric security to mental health support, arts-based empathy building, peer mentoring and community collaboration. It concludes that no one-size-fits-all approach exists and that tailored strategies work best.
one_line: Overview of school safety and anti-bullying programs in six countries, from security technology to arts, mentoring, mental health and community partnerships.
key_facts: Elmwood Elementary in Ontario, Canada, under Principal Anne Thompson, launched 'Operation Respect' on October 3, 2023, engaging students, teachers and parents against bullying.
'Operation Respect' uses workshops, role-playing scenarios and open dialogue forums to turn bystanders into upstanders.

Japan's Tokai City Higashi High School, led by security expert Hiroshi Yamasaki, installed biometric scanners and a real-time location tracking system for all its members (reported November 12, 2023).
Tokai City Higashi High School also introduced an anonymous reporting app for bullying or suspicious behavior without fear of retribution.
Dublin's St. Brigid's Secondary School started the 'Mind Matters' initiative on September 15, 2023, led by counselor Niamh O'Donnell, focused on emotional intelligence and resilience.
'Mind Matters' includes mental health check-ins, mindfulness sessions, teacher training in spotting distress, and a student-led 'Mental Health Ambassadors' peer-support program.

Rio de Janeiro's Escola Futuro Feliz introduced 'Art Against Aggression' on January 22, 2024, led by art teacher Lúcia Freitas, using drama, painting, music and dance to build empathy; bullying incidents decreased significantly.
London's Horizons Academy launched a peer mentoring scheme on December 7, 2023, led by educator Charles Edwards, training upperclassmen to mentor younger students.
Horizons Academy pairs peer mentoring with a leadership program giving students roles of responsibility.
Roseville Area Schools in Minnesota, USA, under Superintendent Mark Johnson, implemented 'Unity in Community' on February 1, 2024, a collaboration of schools, local businesses and law enforcement.
'Unity in Community' features community forums and workshops led by local leaders, police officers and counselors.
The note concludes there is no one-size-fits-all approach; strategies should be tailored to each school's challenges and strengths.
